summary: Focused frontend test of the sendGmail fix in the React app (App.js). Stubbed navigator.canShare/share/clipboard via context.add_init_script across three isolated browser contexts. All 3 test scenarios passed: (T1) Accepted share path with PDF+photo attached, (T2) Fallback path when canShare=false, (T3) AbortError user-cancel path. Also code-verified /app/frontend/public/standalone.html sendGmail — logic matches (shareData without url, AbortError handling, fallback to= param).
critical_code_review_comments: App.js line 522: fallback URL uses ',' (comma) separator via RECIPIENTS.join(',') passed through encodeURIComponent, resulting in to=a%40x%2Cb%40y. Gmail accepts comma-separated recipients so this is correct — verified in T2 opened URL.

standalone_offline.html was not verified at runtime (would need offline serving). Per request note, it is a regenerated mirror of standalone.html with pdf.js embedded; the code diff should be verified by main agent that the offline copy contains the same sendGmail function.
seed_data_creation: Uploaded /tmp/sample.pdf (auto-created 5 notes for WR 17017162 etc.) and a minimal tiny.jpg photo attached to WR 17017162 for T1. Notes persist in DB across T2/T3 contexts (same admin user).

rca of the issue: Fix confirmed: shareData no longer includes a url field so navigator.canShare returns true on Android/iOS where mailto+files was previously rejected. AbortError is properly swallowed without triggering the Gmail Web fallback. When canShare returns false or share throws non-AbortError, fallback opens Gmail compose URL with recipients in to= (not concatenated into body).
